confirmed_bugs.description: mergeDirectKeys uses 'prop in config2' which traverses prototype chain. If Object.prototype is polluted, attacker can inject arbitrary config properties.
confirmed_bugs.fix_description: Guard mergeConfig value reads with hasOwnProp

confirmed_bugs.description: config.socketPath is read without own-property check. Prototype pollution on Object.prototype can inject socketPath to redirect requests to attacker-controlled Unix sockets (SSRF).
confirmed_bugs.fix_description: Guard socketPath with own() to prevent prototype pollution SSRF

confirmed_bugs.description: HTTP adapter reads multiple config properties (proxy, timeout, auth, transport, etc.) without hasOwnProp checks. Polluted Object.prototype can inject any of these.
confirmed_bugs.fix_description: Guard http adapter config reads against prototype pollution

confirmed_bugs.description: formDataToJSON only checks for __proto__ but not constructor/prototype. Attacker can use constructor.prototype to pollute via FormData field names like 'constructor[prototype][polluted]'.
confirmed_bugs.fix_description: Defense-in-depth against already-polluted Object.prototype in formDataToJSON

confirmed_bugs.description: transformResponse accesses this.parseReviver which is inherited from prototype. If Object.prototype.parseReviver is set, all responses will use the attacker's reviver function.
confirmed_bugs.fix_description: Ignore inherited parseReviver and related config reads

confirmed_bugs.description: NO_PROXY hostname normalization bypass. Attacker can craft hostname that bypasses proxy filtering, leading to SSRF against internal services.
confirmed_bugs.fix_description: No_proxy hostname normalization bypass leads to SSRF

confirmed_bugs.description: Headers are set from user-controlled config without sanitization. Attacker can inject CRLF sequences into header values to inject arbitrary headers (cloud metadata exfiltration, cache poisoning).
confirmed_bugs.fix_description: Unrestricted cloud metadata exfiltration via header injection chain

confirmed_bugs.description: When responseType is 'stream', maxContentLength is not enforced on the response stream. Attacker can serve unbounded response data.
confirmed_bugs.fix_description: Stream response bypassed max content length

confirmed_bugs.description: Uses deprecated unescape() function for HTTP basic auth password encoding. This can lead to encoding inconsistencies and potential security issues.
confirmed_bugs.fix_description: Replace deprecated unescape() with modern UTF-8 encoding

confirmed_bugs.description: forEach loop iterates Object.keys({ ...config1, ...config2 }) but the spread operator can include inherited properties if Object.prototype is polluted.
confirmed_bugs.fix_description: More header pollutions — guard config key iteration

confirmed_bugs.description: Malformed XHR upload events (missing loaded/total properties) can cause NaN propagation in progress calculations, leading to incorrect progress reporting.
socket.setKeepAlive called unconditionally without checking if socket exists or is a proxy agent stream. Can cause errors on certain proxy configurations.
confirmed_bugs.fix_description: Guard socket.setKeepAlive for proxy agent streams

known_false_positive_patterns.reason: merge() already blocks __proto__, constructor, prototype on line 409. This is NOT a vulnerability — it's already patched.
Line 100 already returns early for __proto__, constructor, prototype. This is a defense-in-depth measure, not a vulnerability.
The __proto__ check on line 53 is intentional protection. BUG-004 is about missing constructor/prototype checks, NOT about this existing check.
Accessing val.constructor is standard Node.js Buffer detection. Not a vulnerability — val is already validated as non-null object.
Walking prototype chain is intentional for toFlatObject. It's used for merging configs, not for security-sensitive operations.
Object.create(null) cache is safe — no prototype chain. Not a vulnerability.
Object.create(null) for session storage is safe — no prototype chain. Not a vulnerability.
Math.random() token for postMessage is a well-known pattern. Not cryptographically secure but not a vulnerability in this context.

evaluation_notes.bug_density: 12 bugs in ~5000 LOC = 0.24 bugs per 100 LOC
